vars.name: TARGET_URL
vars.description: Beads-viewer base URL to audit. In-pod this is the port-forward tunnel http://localhost:8095 (see gardenio/docs/info-density-audit-harness.md for why the public ingress is unreachable from agent pods). The harness hits {{TARGET_URL}}/u/{{USER_SLUG}} plus its htmx sub-sections.

vars.name: USER_SLUG
vars.description: Canonical homepage slug of a REAL prod operator to audit (e.g. matt-baker). The gardener picks the busiest live operator so the page is exercised with real data. The audit captures /u/{{USER_SLUG}} as the page name 'user-home'.

vars.name: ITERATION
vars.description: Iteration tag (date stamp or fire-time ISO) used as the output directory name under docs/users-cdqr/<ITERATION>/. Used so multiple pours don't collide.

vars.name: PARENT_EPIC
vars.description: Tracking epic for this work. All bug beads filed by the file-issues step are parented here so the operator can browse one tree per dimension.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR+A ({{ITERATION}}): warm up {{TARGET_URL}} and pick/verify the audit user
steps.description:
## Step 1: Boot + Warmup + Pick Audit User

Confirm the audit target is reachable and the user homepage + its htmx sub-sections return < 400 before we burn cycles capturing/measuring.

### Prereq: open a local tunnel + mint a bearer

Follow `gardenio/docs/info-density-audit-harness.md` verbatim: `{{TARGET_URL}}` is expected to be `http://localhost:8095`. Agent pods have no public route to the viewer; port-forward to `svc/gardenio-beads-viewer:8095` and authenticate with a Keycloak `client_credentials` bearer (advice `ka-0000006483`, helper `gardenio/tests/e2e/scripts/lib-keycloak-client-creds.sh`). Also port-forward `svc/gardenio-beads:8080` and bootstrap the operator row via `POST /v1/operators/me/aliases` so authenticated pages render real content instead of the unprovisioned banner.

```bash
export POD_NAMESPACE=${POD_NAMESPACE:-$(cat /var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/namespace 2>/dev/null || echo gardenio)}
export KC_RELEASE_NAME=${KC_RELEASE_NAME:-$POD_NAMESPACE}
# shellcheck disable=SC1091
source gardenio/tests/e2e/scripts/lib-keycloak-client-creds.sh
VIEWER_BEARER=$(mint_client_credentials_token) || { echo 'BLOCKED: bearer mint failed'; exit 1; }
kubectl -n "$POD_NAMESPACE" port-forward svc/gardenio-beads 8080:8080 > /tmp/beads-daemon-pf.log 2>&1 &
BEADS_PF_PID=$!
kubectl -n "$POD_NAMESPACE" port-forward svc/gardenio-beads-viewer 8095:8095 > /tmp/beads-viewer-pf.log 2>&1 &
PF_PID=$!
trap 'kill $PF_PID $BEADS_PF_PID 2>/dev/null || true' EXIT
for i in $(seq 1 30); do curl -fsS -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" "http://localhost:8095/health" && break; sleep 1; done
curl -fsS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"kind":"agent","subject":"gardenio-users-cdqr-audit","source":"audit-bootstrap"}' \
  http://localhost:8080/v1/operators/me/aliases | jq .
```

### Pick the audit user (USER_SLUG is empty by default → you MUST discover one)

The whole point of a *users* page audit is exercising it with a real operator who
has live work. `{{USER_SLUG}}` ships empty so the gardener always audits a
currently-busy human. Discover the slug from the **live `/people` directory** —
NOT from `/agents` (its rows render no per-user links) and NOT by guessing
(`matt-baker`, `matthew.baker`, etc. all 404; real slugs are dotted full names
like `sam.rivers`, `al.kent`).

Verified routing facts (2026-06-17, confirmed against the in-cluster viewer):
- The app serves user homepages at **`/u/<slug>`** at the service root. A `200`
  from `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" {{TARGET_URL}}/u/<slug>`
  is the only proof a slug is valid.
- `/people` hrefs are rendered with a **`/beads` reverse-proxy prefix**
  (`href="/beads/u/sam.rivers"`). Strip the `/beads` prefix before hitting
  `{{TARGET_URL}}` — `/beads/u/<slug>` 404s against the port-forward; `/u/<slug>` is 200.
- Real human slugs are dotted full names. `op-<id>` slugs are operator sentinels
  (still 200 but thin) — prefer a dotted human slug with live work.

```bash
# 1. Pull candidate slugs from the live directory, stripping the /beads prefix.
mapfile -t SLUGS < <(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER"   "{{TARGET_URL}}/people"   | grep -oE 'href="/beads/u/[^"]+"' | sed -E 's|href="/beads/u/||;s|"||'   | grep -vE '^(op-|group_|e2e-fixture|info-density-audit|gardenio2)'   | sort -u)
printf '%s
' "${SLUGS[@]}" | head -40

# 2. Rank by live homepage work: the operator whose /u/<slug> has the most
#    non-empty sections is the best stress test. Cheap proxy: count rendered
#    bead rows + "(N)" count chips on each candidate's page; pick the max.
best=""; best_n=-1
for s in "${SLUGS[@]}"; do
  html=$(curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" "{{TARGET_URL}}/u/$s")
  [ -z "$html" ] && continue
  n=$(printf '%s' "$html" | grep -oE 'class="bead-row|\([0-9]+\)' | wc -l)
  printf '%-30s rows~%s
' "$s" "$n"
  if [ "$n" -gt "$best_n" ]; then best_n=$n; best=$s; fi
done
echo "CHOSEN: $best (signal=$best_n)"
```

Prefer the operator-of-record (Matt Baker / `oidc:matthew.baker@acme.example`) IF a
dotted slug for them resolves 200; he has none today, so fall back to the busiest
dotted human slug from the ranking above. Record the chosen slug in a comment and
pass it forward as `{{USER_SLUG}}` — downstream steps (capture/measure/judge/file/report)
read it from this step's comment. Set `SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG=<chosen>` before the
capture step.

### Verify the page + sub-sections

With `VIEWER_BEARER` set, all of these must be < 400:

```bash
for path in "/u/${USER_SLUG}" \
            "/u/${USER_SLUG}/section/forwarded" \
            "/u/${USER_SLUG}/section/recent-comments" \
            "/u/${USER_SLUG}/status-message"; do
  code=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" "{{TARGET_URL}}${path}")
  printf '%-48s -> %s\n' "$path" "$code"
done
```

### Deliverables (post as comments, then close)
- Comment: chosen audit slug + how it was selected (busiest / operator-of-record).
- Comment: per-path HTTP status table.
- Comment: 'PASS' or per-path failure detail.

If the main page returns >= 400, do NOT close — file a bug parented to {{PARENT_EPIC}} and BLOCK (comment 'BLOCKED' and stop). A broken homepage is itself the highest-severity Correctness finding.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR ({{ITERATION}}): capture screenshots + DOM for /u/{{USER_SLUG}}
steps.description:
## Step 2: Capture

Run the Playwright harness against `{{TARGET_URL}}` for the chosen user homepage and store output under `docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/`. The harness already injects `Authorization: Bearer $BEADS_VIEWER_BEARER` as an extraHTTPHeader, and the spec captures `/u/{slug}` as page `user-home` when `SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG` is set (ka-0000000737).

### Steps
1. Re-establish the tunnel + bearer (prereq block in step 1). Export under both names the harness reads:
   ```bash
   export BEADS_VIEWER_BEARER=$VIEWER_BEARER
   export SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG=<slug-from-step-1>
   ```
2. Branch off fresh main:
   ```bash
   git fetch origin && git checkout main && git pull --ff-only
   git checkout -b chore/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}
   ```
3. Run the harness (captures all canonical pages incl. user-home; we keep only user-home):
   ```bash
   BEADS_VIEWER_URL='{{TARGET_URL}}' make screenshot-beads-viewer
   ```
   Output: `gardenio/tests/beads-viewer-screenshots/test-results/beads-viewer-screenshots/{desktop,narrow}/user-home.{png,html}`.
4. Also fetch the raw rendered HTML for the page AND each htmx sub-section (the page lazy-loads forwarded + recent-comments), so the measure/judge steps see real DOM:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/html
   for spec in "user-home:/u/${SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG}" \
               "section-forwarded:/u/${SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG}/section/forwarded" \
               "section-recent-comments:/u/${SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG}/section/recent-comments"; do
     slug=${spec%%:*}; path=${spec#*:}
     curl -fsSL -H "Authorization: Bearer $VIEWER_BEARER" "{{TARGET_URL}}${path}" \
       -o "docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/html/${slug}.html"
   done
   ```
5. Move screenshots into the run dir:
   ```bash
   mkdir -p docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/screenshots/{desktop,narrow}
   for vp in desktop narrow; do
     cp gardenio/tests/beads-viewer-screenshots/test-results/beads-viewer-screenshots/$vp/user-home.png \
        docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/screenshots/$vp/ 2>/dev/null || true
   done
   ```
6. Commit:
   ```bash
   git add docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/
   git commit -m "chore(users-cdqr): capture {{ITERATION}} for /u/${SCREENSHOT_USER_SLUG}"
   ```

### Deliverables
- Branch `chore/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}` with `captures/{html,screenshots}/` populated.
- Comment: `du -sh` of captures + commit SHA + confirmation both desktop & narrow PNGs exist.

If the harness fails, root-cause it (check `/tmp/beads-viewer-pf.log` for a dead port-forward, re-mint the bearer if it expired) and BLOCK.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR+A ({{ITERATION}}): compute objective metrics for the five dimensions
steps.description:
## Step 3: Measure (objective; no judgement)

Reuse the density measure helper AND compute correctness/relevance signals from the DOM. The existing `gardenio/tests/beads-viewer-screenshots/tools/measure-density.py` already emits DOM + pixel metrics per page; run it over the captures dir to get the **Density** vector. Then layer a CDQR-specific pass.

### Density (reuse measure-density.py)
Per the html + png metrics it already computes: `dom_element_count`, `text_byte_count`, `text_byte_per_dom`, `unique_links`, `data_fields`, and per-screenshot `near_white_ratio`, `mean_luma`, `pixel_count`.

### Correctness signals (grep the captured HTML)
For `captures/html/user-home.html` (and the two section partials):
| Signal | How to compute |
| --- | --- |
| `error_markers` | count of `error`, `failed to`, `nil`, `panic`, `unprovisioned`, `no operator`, HTTP 5xx banners (case-insensitive grep) |
| `empty_section_markers` | count of empty-state strings (`No items`, `Nothing here`, `0 results`, empty `<tbody></tbody>`) |
| `broken_links` | count of `href="#"`, `href=""`, `href="/u/"` (slug-less), or obvious template-leak `{{` in href |
| `template_leaks` | count of literal `{{` / `}}` / `<no value>` rendered into the body (Go template mis-render) |
| `htmx_unresolved` | count of `hx-get` placeholders whose partial returned empty in the section fetches |

Any `template_leaks > 0` or `error_markers > 0` is an automatic Correctness fail flag — record it.

### Relevance signals (which homepage sections actually carried content)
The homepage sections (from `user_home.go`): pinned, active-agents, open-decisions, recent-comments, open-mrs, recent-commits, recent-merged, forwarded-mentions, their-automations. For each, detect presence + non-empty row count by section heading + following list/table:
| Signal | How to compute |
| --- | --- |
| `sections_present` | list of section slugs whose heading rendered |
| `sections_nonempty` | subset that rendered >= 1 data row |
| `top_fold_section` | the first section by DOM order (proxy for what the user sees first) |

### Output
Write a CDQR-specific helper `gardenio/tests/beads-viewer-screenshots/tools/measure-cdqr.py` that ingests the captures dir and emits `docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/metrics.json`:
```json
{
  "target_url": "{{TARGET_URL}}", "user_slug": "<slug>", "iteration": "{{ITERATION}}",
  "density": { "desktop": {"near_white_ratio": 0.0, "data_fields": 0, "dom_element_count": 0, "text_byte_per_dom": 0.0}, "narrow": {} },
  "correctness": {"error_markers": 0, "empty_section_markers": 0, "broken_links": 0, "template_leaks": 0, "htmx_unresolved": 0},
  "relevance": {"sections_present": [], "sections_nonempty": [], "top_fold_section": ""}
}
```
Commit the helper + metrics.json on the branch.

### Deliverables
- `measure-cdqr.py` + `metrics.json` committed.
- Comment: compact table of the headline numbers per dimension.
- If a screenshot is unreadable, mark its block `null` and warn — do not BLOCK (the judge skips nulls).

### Accomplishment signals (A — "what they've actually DONE")

This is the **headline dimension** for this gardener. The operator's complaint is
that the page does a terrible job of showing what a person *has actually done*.
So `measure` must quantify how legible completed/shipped work is on the page.

A person's *accomplishments* live in these homepage sections + any top band:
`recent-merged` (merged MRs / closed work), `recent-commits` (landed commits),
`open-mrs` only counts as in-flight, NOT done. Closed beads, resolved decisions,
and shipped releases are accomplishments too.

For `captures/html/user-home.html` (+ the section partials) compute:

| Signal | How to compute |
| --- | --- |
| `accomplishment_summary_present` | bool — is there a page-level *done-work* aggregate band near the top (e.g. a stat strip reading "N merged · M commits · K beads closed (14d)")? grep the head of `<main>` for an aggregate/stat container that names completed work. Absent today ⇒ false. |
| `done_signal_fields` | count of rendered data points that convey *completed* work: rows under `recent-merged` + rows under `recent-commits` + any "closed"/"merged"/"shipped"/"resolved" count chips. |
| `recency_windows_present` | list of time windows the page surfaces for activity (e.g. `7d`, `14d`, `30d`, `all-time`). grep section headings + chips for `\b\d+d\b` / `today` / `this week`. |
| `done_vs_inflight_separated` | bool — are *done* sections (recent-merged, recent-commits) visually/structurally distinct from *in-flight* ones (open-mrs, open-decisions, active-agents)? Heuristic: are the done sections grouped/labeled as accomplishments rather than interleaved with todo work? |
| `accomplishment_top_fold` | bool — is at least one done-work signal above the fold (within the first ~900px of DOM order / before the first in-flight section)? |

Add an `accomplishment` block to `metrics.json`:
```json
"accomplishment": {
  "accomplishment_summary_present": false,
  "done_signal_fields": 0,
  "recency_windows_present": [],
  "done_vs_inflight_separated": false,
  "accomplishment_top_fold": false
}
```
Extend `measure-cdqr.py` to emit this block alongside density/correctness/relevance.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR+A ({{ITERATION}}): score Correctness / Density / Quality / Relevance / Accomplishment-Legibility
steps.description:
## Step 4: Judge — the CDQR+A rubric

Produce a 0-10 score + verdict for each of the **five** dimensions, combining the
objective metrics (step 3) with a visual review of the screenshots. **You MUST
visually inspect** `docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/screenshots/desktop/user-home.png`
(and narrow) with the Read tool — the screenshot is the source of truth; metrics
only triage.

> **Headline dimension:** This gardener exists because the operator said the page
> "does a terrible job of showing what they've actually done." **A —
> Accomplishment Legibility** is the dimension that encodes that complaint. The
> page cannot score well overall while a person's completed work is invisible,
> buried, or indistinguishable from their backlog — no matter how clean it looks.

### The five dimensions

**C — Correctness** (is what's shown true and unbroken?)
- Any `template_leaks > 0`, `error_markers > 0`, or 5xx in a section ⇒ score <= 3 (broken).
- Broken/slug-less links, htmx sections that never resolve, stale or obviously-wrong counts ⇒ deduct.
- Visual: does the rendered page match what the DOM claims? Garbled rows, overlapping text, misattributed names ⇒ Correctness, not Quality.
- 10 = every datum accurate, every link works, every section resolves.

**D — Density** (signal per pixel — Tufte)
- Anchor on `near_white_ratio` (desktop): >= 0.55 ⇒ <= 4; 0.40-0.55 ⇒ 5-6; 0.25-0.40 ⇒ 7-8; < 0.25 with readable layout ⇒ 9-10.
- Cross-check `data_fields` and `dom_element_count`: a page with acres of blank and < 25 data fields is sparse regardless.
- Penalize wasteful whitespace; do NOT penalize functional gutters/margins.

**Q — Quality** (craft & polish)
- Visual: alignment, consistent spacing, typographic hierarchy, no overflow/clipping, narrow viewport doesn't break the layout, section headers are scannable.
- Penalize: misaligned columns, inconsistent card styling, text running under/over elements, unstyled raw lists, jarring color use.
- 10 = looks designed, not assembled.

**R — Relevance** (is THIS the right content for a *user homepage*?)
- A user's homepage should answer 'what is mine and what needs me, right now?' Expected high-value sections: pinned, open-decisions (needs-you), active-agents (my running work), open-mrs, recent-comments, forwarded-mentions, their-automations.
- Use `sections_present` / `sections_nonempty` / `top_fold_section` from metrics: is the most decision-relevant content above the fold? Are empty sections hogging prime real estate while live work is buried?
- Penalize: irrelevant-to-this-user content, important sections below the fold or absent, ordering that doesn't match urgency.
- 10 = opening this page tells the user exactly what to do next.

**A — Accomplishment Legibility** (HEADLINE — does the page show what this person has actually DONE?)
- The core test: a stranger lands on `/u/{slug}`. Within ~5 seconds and without scrolling, can they answer *"what has this person actually accomplished, and recently?"* If not, A is weak.
- Anchor on metrics: `accomplishment_summary_present`, `done_signal_fields`, `recency_windows_present`, `done_vs_inflight_separated`, `accomplishment_top_fold`.
- Score bands:
  - `accomplishment_summary_present == false` AND `accomplishment_top_fold == false` ⇒ **score <= 3**. (Today's likely state: done-work is a couple of mid/low-page lists with no aggregate — this is exactly the complaint.)
  - A few done rows exist but there is no aggregate band, no recency framing, and done is interleaved with in-flight ⇒ 4-5.
  - Done sections present, distinct from in-flight, but no top-of-page "what they've shipped" summary ⇒ 6-7.
  - A scannable accomplishment summary band (counts + recency windows) above the fold, clearly separating shipped work from backlog ⇒ 8-9.
  - Plus per-window trends / a contribution timeline / a legible "impact" framing ⇒ 10.
- Visual cues to reward: a stat strip of completed work, "merged/closed/shipped (Nd)" chips, a contribution/activity timeline, clear "Done" vs "In flight" grouping, links from a count to the underlying beads/MRs.
- Visual cues to penalize: completed work shown only as undifferentiated bead rows mixed with open work; no counts; no time framing; accomplishments below the fold while empty in-flight sections sit up top.

### Output
`docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/verdicts.json`:
```json
{
  "iteration": "{{ITERATION}}", "user_slug": "<slug>",
  "scores": {
    "correctness":    {"score": 0, "verdict": "broken|weak|ok|good|excellent", "observations": "...", "issues": ["..."], "recommendations": ["..."]},
    "density":        {"score": 0, "verdict": "...", "observations": "...", "issues": [], "recommendations": []},
    "quality":        {"score": 0, "verdict": "...", "observations": "...", "issues": [], "recommendations": []},
    "relevance":      {"score": 0, "verdict": "...", "observations": "...", "issues": [], "recommendations": []},
    "accomplishment": {"score": 0, "verdict": "...", "observations": "...", "issues": [], "recommendations": []}
  },
  "overall": {"score": 0.0, "headline": "one-line state-of-the-users-page"}
}
```
Score bands: 0-3 broken, 4-5 weak, 6-7 ok, 8-9 good, 10 excellent.
`overall.score` = mean of the **five** dimensions. If A < 5, the headline MUST name
the accomplishment gap explicitly (that is the operator's stated pain).

### Deliverables
- `verdicts.json` committed on the branch.
- Comment: a 5-row scorecard (dimension | score | verdict | top recommendation) + the one-line headline.
- Full `verdicts.json` pasted into a comment for the file-issues step.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR+A ({{ITERATION}}): file bug beads per low-scoring dimension
steps.description:
## Step 5: File Issues

For every of the **five** dimensions in `verdicts.json` scoring **<= 6** (weak or broken), file ONE bug bead with that dimension's concrete recommendations. A 7+ dimension does not get a bug (it's at least 'ok').

### Per-dimension bug bead
```bash
kd create "Users page CDQR: <Dimension> scored <N>/10 — <one-line>" \
  --type=bug --project=gardenio -p 2 \
  -l project:gardenio -l area:beads-viewer -l kind:users-cdqr -l "cdqr:<dimension>"   # dimension ∈ correctness|density|quality|relevance|accomplishment \
  --description "## CDQR audit context

Iteration: {{ITERATION}}
Target: {{TARGET_URL}}/u/<slug>
Dimension: <Correctness|Density|Quality|Relevance>
Score: <N>/10  (verdict: <verdict>)

## Observations
<verbatim from verdicts.json>

## Issues
- <bullet>

## Recommended fixes
- <bullet>

## Evidence
- Desktop: docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/screenshots/desktop/user-home.png
- Narrow:  docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/captures/screenshots/narrow/user-home.png
- Metrics: docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/metrics.json

parent({{PARENT_EPIC}})"
```

### Priority: the Accomplishment dimension is the headline
When filing the **accomplishment** bug, set `-p 1` (not 2) and prefix the title
`Users page: accomplishments are illegible —` so it sorts to the top of the epic.
This is the operator's explicit complaint; it should not get lost among polish bugs.

### Deduplication (per dimension)
Before filing, search for an open bead with the same dimension scope:
```bash
kd list --status=open -l kind:users-cdqr -l "cdqr:<dimension>"   # dimension ∈ correctness|density|quality|relevance|accomplishment 2>&1
```
If one exists, comment the new iteration's score + evidence on it (reference both iterations) instead of filing a duplicate. If the dimension has recovered to 7+ this iteration, comment that on the open bead and propose closing it.

### Deliverables
- Comment listing each filed-or-updated bug bead ID + its dimension + score.
- If all five dimensions score 7+, comment 'All five CDQR+A dimensions >= 7 this iteration — nothing to file 🎉' and close the step.
- Do NOT close {{PARENT_EPIC}} — the report step rolls up first.

steps.title: Users-page CDQR+A ({{ITERATION}}): publish roll-up report and land MR
steps.description:
## Step 6: Report + Land MR

Produce a rolled-up report on {{PARENT_EPIC}} and land captures+metrics+verdicts on main via an MR so future iterations can diff.

### Steps
1. Build `docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/REPORT.md`:
   - Header: iteration, target, audited slug, date.
   - **CDQR+A scorecard**: 5-row table — dimension | score/10 | verdict | filed bug bead. (Accomplishment-Legibility row first.)
   - Headline + overall score.
   - Inline-embed the desktop screenshot.
   - Trends: if a previous `docs/users-cdqr/<previous>/verdicts.json` exists, diff each dimension's score and flag deltas >= 1.0 (regression or recovery).
   - Index of bug beads filed/updated this iteration.
2. Commit + push + open MR:
   ```bash
   git add docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/REPORT.md
   git commit -m "chore(users-cdqr): {{ITERATION}} roll-up report"
   git push -u origin chore/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}
   glab mr create \
     --title "chore(users-cdqr): {{ITERATION}} audit (overall <N>/10)" \
     --description "Automated Users-Page CDQR audit for {{TARGET_URL}}/u/<slug>.\n\nReport: docs/users-cdqr/{{ITERATION}}/REPORT.md\nParent: {{PARENT_EPIC}}\nOperator: Matt Baker" \
     --remove-source-branch --squash-before-merge
   gb mr link <this-bead-id> <mr-url>
   ```
3. Wait for CI green; on transient flake, retrigger via the pipeline API (NEVER close/reopen — global advice).
4. Self-merge once green (gardenio repo, pre-authorized — advice ka-0000002230).
5. Comment on {{PARENT_EPIC}}:
   ```
   CDQR iteration {{ITERATION}} complete. User: /u/<slug>
   Scores — A:<n> C:<n> D:<n> Q:<n> R:<n>  (overall <n>/10)
   Bug beads: <list>
   Report: <permalink at merge SHA>
   ```
6. Close this step bead. The schedule trigger fires the next iteration on cadence.
